item.title: 0.6.0-beta.5
item.description:
# Agent HUD 0.6.0-beta.5
## Compatibility
**Requires Agent HUD for iPhone 1.7.2 or later** for iPhone and Apple Watch sync. Update the iPhone app before updating the Mac. Older iPhone versions cannot read this release's data.
[Get the iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812113619).
If the required iPhone version is not yet on the App Store, cross-device features require the corresponding TestFlight version.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
## Changes
### Coming from 0.5.5
- Includes everything in [0.6.0-beta.1](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.1), which moves Agent HUD to a new cross-platform app and brings your settings and 30 days of quota history with it, and the changes in [0.6.0-beta.2](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.2), [0.6.0-beta.3](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.3) and [0.6.0-beta.4](https://github.com/jazzenchen/agent-hud-open/releases/tag/v0.6.0-beta.4).
### New
- Adds Agent HUD's plugin for DeepSeek Harness, on the DeepSeek Harness card in Settings → Agent plugins. Every Harness host loads it at once, the Desktop app included, and it stays up to date at launch. With it: - Harness's questions and approvals reach the HUD beside Harness's own cards. Whichever is answered first wins, and the other card goes away. - Agents, this Mac and your phone can message Harness sessions. A message waits as the session's next message and never interrupts a turn. "Send messages" on the plugin's row turns this off. - The session page shows Harness's replies, which it never did, without its reasoning or the context Harness adds to each prompt. - Agent messages come back properly: the recipient is asked to reply with Agent HUD's send_message, a reply marks the message as replied, and the paper plane flies back once, only with a reply or an answer it can read. - Adds the HUD tools to Cursor, DeepSeek Harness and Antigravity. Adding them for any client also installs the customize-agent-hud skill, which teaches the agent how to change the HUD; removing them takes it away, and it is brought up to date at launch. - Draws each turn's sub-agents as a timeline on the session page: name, type, when each started and was last heard from. Running ones pulse. - Rebuilds Settings on one set of sections and rows: - The sidebar is in groups: General and Display; Agents, Agent plugins, Relays and Prices; Remote, Local Network and Subscription; then Updates. - General has appearance and language, usage display, startup and the menu bar icon. - Display has one preview for every mode, the glow sliders behind Fine-tune, panel density with the panel, hover and logo settings under All screens, and the undo and reset rows in a Reset section at the bottom. - Agents keeps its list in place while you scroll, with agents not on this computer below the rest. - Agent plugins is a page of its own: client hooks first, then a folding card per client with its status, opened only when something needs you. - Relays and Prices lose their repeated headings. Prices fold per agent and open where a model has no price. - Remote lists only the agents Remote serves that are on this Mac. "Send from this Mac" and the iCloud details fold away. - Local Network is one sharing card, then pairing, then your devices with their online status. - Every menu is drawn by Agent HUD; the relay form's type and currency menus used the system's own. - Descriptions are one short line, and only where a title alone could mislead. - Settings shows a centered spinner while it loads, and Retry only after a failure. - Gives Settings → Subscription one switch for this Mac, as the Swift app had: - Turning it on uses your saved key, else an App Store seat; after you release this Mac's seat you no longer have to type the key again. - Turning it off gives back every seat this Mac holds. - Seats add up across the key and the App Store subscription, and a full key gives way to a free App Store seat. When neither has room, the page asks which Mac to take offline. - A refused activation shows the store's own reason, and the list of your Macs comes from your account's own records. - Shows every DeepSeek balance currency in the HUD, not only the first one, which could be an empty USD balance beside a CNY one. Settings → Agents lets you hide balances and change their order. - Reads the DeepSeek Platform account that DeepSeek Harness signs in to: its topped-up balance, and its granted balance while there is one. - Lets you choose which Codex models the token chart shows, and in what order, in Settings → Agents → Codex. The list is the models used in the past 30 days, and new models appear on their own. Agents can change it through the HUD tools too. - Reads Grok Bot's weekly quota from Cursor's servers when Cursor is signed in to the same account, so it no longer goes stale when the Bot is not used on this Mac. An account merged into SuperGrok shows its plan, "Super", as the Bot does. An old reading says it is more than a day old and that opening Grok Bot refreshes it. - Reads a Cursor account merged into SuperGrok from the weekly period Cursor shows, so its rings move instead of staying at 0%. - Prices GPT-6.1 Terra.
### Fixes
- Sends to Antigravity through the service that can open the conversation. Before, a conversation not opened since Antigravity started was refused, and a message failed whenever an empty Antigravity service, such as a fresh window, ran beside the one that has the chat. - Reaches Antigravity sessions by the id the HUD lists. A message carries the model its conversation last ran with; a new conversation takes your default model. - Starts Antigravity sessions on Antigravity 2.26, which refused them, and shows the Antigravity service's own error instead of a generic one. - Keeps the MCP relay's tools in step with the app: a tool group switched on later reaches Antigravity and DeepSeek Harness in their next turn, without a restart. - Looks up a client's command line again at launch when the saved one is missing or gone, so messages to Codex conversations are no longer refused. - Names every window Agent HUD; some were still called Agent HUD Next. - Says, for each system, why HUD tools can't be added from a copy of Agent HUD outside its install location. - Draws the HUD rim with WebGPU directly.

# Agent HUD 0.5.5
## Compatibility
**Requires Agent HUD for iPhone 1.5 or later** for iPhone and Apple Watch sync. Update the iPhone app before updating the Mac. Older iPhone versions cannot read this release's data.
[Get the iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812113619).
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
## Changes
### Quota names on every device
- Keeps quota window names and short forms in English, so an English iPhone, widget or Apple Watch no longer receives Chinese names from a Mac using Chinese. Names update after the Mac reads and syncs the account again.
### Docks and appearance
- Keeps every logo visible on Simple and Dynamic docks while a reply or request opens beside the sending agent's logo. - Gives each display its own dark, light or system appearance, solid or glass material and transparency. Settings → General can match windows to their display's HUD as an experimental option. - Lets both dock sizes run from 20 to 60 pt, adds Simple panel logo spacing and uses one smaller text size for dock numbers, reminders and the hover line. - Makes the agents' bots act out thinking, tools, approvals, questions, plans, compaction, failures and usage limits. Claude's bot is Clawd. - Keeps the menu bar's figure, colours and agent order in step with the main display's HUD and its layout.
### Arrange the HUD with an agent
- Adds client checkmarks and add/remove actions for the MCP server in Settings → Experimental. - Names the tools `get_hud`, `get_hud_screenshot`, `draft_hud`, `discard_hud_draft` and `finish_hud_edit`. The server remains `agent-hud`; turn on the renamed HUD tools switch again to use it. - Lets an agent filter sessions by project and period, choose block accounts and row order, change panel switches and propose app settings as a draft for you to save. - Holds the panel open while an agent arranges it, then lets go when the edit finishes or you dismiss it. - Adds balance burn rates, estimated run-out times and cost charts to API balance blocks.
### Sessions and other agents
- Removes archived or deleted sessions from session lists while keeping their tokens in the usage totals until the ledger expires them. - Lets a session using a tool take over an agent's mark from one that is thinking. - Answers Claude Code plan approvals on the HUD, including accepting edits or returning feedback to keep planning. - Ends Claude Code turns promptly when their logs report a usage limit or API failure. - Keeps one provider order across Settings, the HUD, glow, menu bar and token statistics. - Shows WorkBuddy's model ceilings and credits, reads a GLM plan held only by WorkBuddy under that group and handles a CodeBuddy CLI using WorkBuddy's configuration as WorkBuddy. - Reduces artwork memory, repeated island layout and process inspection for clients that are not installed.
### iPhone and Apple Watch sync
- Sends Claude's narrations and questions to the phone, including questions answered through the Claude desktop app's next-step box. - Keeps published turn text once and improves local-network change tracking and conversation-cache recovery. - Ships the Mac executable stripped and the updater for Apple Silicon only, while keeping debugging symbols locally for crash reports.
